problems.title: A derivative at one
problems.question: Find f′(1) for f(x)=ln x/eˣ.
problems.idea: Write f=e^{−x}ln x and use the product rule.
steps: At x=1 the bracket equals 1.

problems.title: A fifth-root product’s decreasing interval
problems.question: Find where f(x)=⁵√[(x+3)⁴]·(x−2)⁵ decreases.
problems.idea: Keep the sign when differentiating the absolute-value power.
formulas: For x≠−3, the sign of f′ is the sign of (x+3)(29x+67), apart from the nonnegative factor (x−2)⁴.
steps: Both factors are negative for x<−3, so the derivative is positive.
For −3<x<−67/29 the signs differ, so it is negative. For x>−67/29 it is nonnegative.
Continuity permits including the two endpoints of the decreasing segment.

problems.title: A standard exponential limit
problems.question: Find limₙ→∞(1+3/(2n))^{n+2}.
problems.idea: Use the definition of e with a scaled exponent.
steps: Split off the last two factors: [(1+3/(2n))ⁿ](1+3/(2n))².
The factors tend to e^{3/2} and 1.

problems.title: A sine limit with an inner cosine
problems.question: Find limₓ→π/2 sin²(cos x)/cos²x.
problems.idea: Set u=cos x, which tends to zero.
steps: The quotient is (sin u/u)² for u≠0.
Its limit is 1.

problems.title: A directrix leaves a vertical-position ambiguity
problems.question: A parabola lies to the right of directrix x=1. Its focus-to-directrix distance equals the distance from (−3,2) to 3x+4y=4. Find its equation.
problems.idea: Compute that distance, then use the focus/directrix definition.
steps: The focus therefore has x-coordinate 2, with arbitrary y-coordinate k. The vertex is (3/2,k).
The focal distance from the vertex is 1/2, so the equation is (y−k)²=2(x−3/2).
If the intended axis is the x-axis, set k=0 and obtain y²=2x−3.
problems.note: The focus’s vertical coordinate is not specified, and none of the printed equations matches even the x-axis-centred case.

problems.title: The angle between an axis and a plane
problems.question: Find the acute angle between the x-axis and x−5y+3z−8=0.
problems.idea: Use the normal vector of the plane.
steps: The numerator is 1 and |n|=√35.

problems.title: An ellipse inscribed in a rectangle
problems.question: Find the axis-aligned ellipse inscribed in the rectangle x=4,x=10,y=−3,y=7.
problems.idea: Its centre is the rectangle centre, and its semiaxes are half the side lengths.
steps: Insert these into the standard ellipse equation.

problems.title: A hyperbola from asymptotes and one focus
problems.question: The diagonals of the rectangle x=4,x=10,y=−3,y=7 are a hyperbola’s asymptotes. One focus lies on x=10. Find its equation.
problems.idea: The centre and asymptote slope come from the rectangle.
formulas: Centre=(7,2); b/a=5/3; focal distance c=3; c²=a²+b².
steps: Put a²=9t,b²=25t. Then 34t=9, so a²=81/34,b²=225/34.
The horizontal-axis hyperbola therefore satisfies (x−7)²/81−(y−2)²/225=1/34.

problems.title: An insphere in a square-base pyramid
problems.question: A pyramid has square base of side 1 and height 1 along a lateral edge. Find its insphere radius.
problems.idea: Use volume and total surface area.
steps: Volume=1/3. Base area=1. Two lateral faces have area 1/2 each; the other two have area √2/2 each.
Thus S_total=2+√2 and r=1/(2+√2).
Rationalize the denominator.
problems.note: The source calls this a “triangular pyramid” while specifying a square base. The computation follows the square-base geometry described.

problems.title: Tangents from the centre of a hyperbola
problems.question: A hyperbola has foci on the x-axis and the y-axis as a symmetry axis. How many tangents can be drawn from the origin?
problems.idea: These conditions place the hyperbola centre at the origin.
formulas: For x²/a²−y²/b²=1, a tangent at (x₀,y₀) is xx₀/a²−yy₀/b²=1.
steps: Substituting the origin into any tangent equation gives 0=1, impossible.
The asymptotes pass through the origin but are not tangents at finite curve points.

problems.title: A diagonal-section plane of a box
problems.question: A box has a vertex at the origin, edges on the axes, and opposite vertex (2,1,3). Which listed plane is a diagonal section not passing through the origin?
problems.idea: Join opposite vertical edges over the base diagonal from (2,0) to (0,1).
steps: Extending it vertically gives x+2y−2=0.
It contains full opposite edges of the box and does not contain the origin.

problems.title: Maximize a squared vector distance
problems.question: Given a²+b²=6 and c²+d²=8, maximize (a−c)²+(b−d)².
problems.idea: The vectors have fixed lengths √6 and √8.
steps: The maximum squared distance is (√6+√8)²=14+8√3.
It is attained by choosing the two vectors in opposite directions.

problems.title: An exponential integral by substitution
problems.question: Evaluate $\int_0^1 0.5x\,e^{x^2}\,dx$.
problems.idea: Set u=x².
steps: The bounds become 0 and 1. The integral is (1/4)[eᵘ]₀¹.

problems.title: A range through a squared substitution
problems.question: Find the range of y=(x−1)²√(x²−2x+3) for 0≤x≤1.5.
problems.idea: Set t=(x−1)².
steps: Both nonnegative factors increase with t, so their product increases on [0,1].
The minimum is 0 and maximum √3, both attained.

problems.title: The minimum of a sixth-power trig sum
problems.question: Find the minimum of sin⁶x+cos⁶x.
problems.idea: Treat sin²x and cos²x as numbers whose sum is 1.
steps: The expression is 1−3sin²x cos²x≥1−3/4.
Equality occurs when sin²x=cos²x=1/2.

problems.title: A chord’s midpoint on a tangent line
problems.question: The tangent to y=1/(1−x) at M=(2,−1) intersects y=−a²x²+5ax−4 in two points whose midpoint is M. Find a.
problems.idea: Find the tangent, then use the sum of the intersection roots.
formulas: Tangent slope=1, so y=x−3; intersection equation a²x²−(5a−1)x+1=0.
steps: Midpoint x-coordinate 2 requires the root sum to be 4: (5a−1)/a²=4.
This gives a=1 or 1/4. The a=0 case is not a quadratic and cannot produce two intersections.
For a=1, x²−4x+1=0 has two real roots. For a=1/4 the discriminant is negative.

problems.title: Equal positive intercepts of a plane
problems.question: A plane passes through (5,2,3) and cuts equal positive lengths from all three axes. Find their sum.
problems.idea: Use intercept form.
steps: Substitute the point: (5+2+3)/L=1, so L=10.
There are three intercept lengths.

problems.title: A plane parallel to two vectors
problems.question: Find the plane through the origin parallel to (4,−1,2) and (3,2,−5).
problems.idea: Their cross product is a normal.
steps: The plane through the origin with that normal is x+26y+11z=0.
Both given vectors have dot product zero with the normal.

problems.title: A slant asymptote by polynomial division
problems.question: Find the slant asymptote of y=(x²+4x+3)/(4−x).
problems.idea: Separate a linear term and a vanishing remainder.
steps: The last fraction tends to zero as x→±∞.

problems.title: An elliptical section touching both cylinder bases
problems.question: A cylinder has radius 1 and height 2. An oblique section is an ellipse tangent to both base circles. Find its area.
problems.idea: The plane rises by 2 across a base diameter of length 2.
formulas: Its inclination is 45°; orthogonal projected area=ellipse area·cos45°.
steps: The ellipse projects to the unit disk, area π.
Therefore the section area is π/cos45°=√2π.

problems.title: Shortest canal between a parabola and a line
problems.question: The river paths are y=x² and x−y−2=0. Find the shortest connecting segment.
problems.idea: Minimize point-to-line distance over the parabola.
steps: The square is minimized at x=1/2.
The minimum distance is 7/(4√2).

problems.title: A local maximum with a logarithmic domain
problems.question: Find the local-maximum input of y=2ln(x−2)−x²+4x+1.
problems.idea: Use x>2 and solve the derivative equation.
steps: Set t=x−2>0. Then y′=2(1/t−t), which changes from positive to negative at t=1.
Thus x=3 is a local maximum; its function value is 4.

problems.title: An ellipse and a hyperbola with common foci
problems.question: A=(1,3), B=(5,3). One locus has PA+PB=5; another has |PA−PB|=3. How many intersection points are there?
problems.idea: Solve for the two distances.
steps: For PA=4,PB=1, the two circles have centre distance 4. Since |4−1|<4<4+1, they intersect in two points.
Swapping the two distances gives two more reflected points.
The two sets are distinct because the distances are different.
problems.note: This uses the usual absolute difference defining both hyperbola branches. A signed difference PA−PB=3 would select one branch and give 2 intersections.

problems.title: Count tangents with a prescribed intercept ratio
problems.question: For y=x³−3x²−7x+6, count points whose tangent cuts a positive x-intercept and a negative y-intercept twice as long.
problems.idea: Such a tangent must have slope 2 and negative y-intercept.
formulas: A line with intercepts p>0 and −2p has equation y=2x−2p.
steps: Set f′=3x²−6x−7=2. The candidate contact inputs are x=3 and x=−1.
At x=3, the tangent intercept is f(3)−2·3=−21, which is negative.
At x=−1 it is f(−1)+2=11, which fails the sign condition.

problems.title: The largest inradius at fixed triangle area
problems.question: Among isosceles triangles of a fixed area S, which apex angle maximizes the inradius?
problems.idea: Since r=S/s, minimize semiperimeter s.
formulas: Heron and AM–GM give S²≤s⁴/27, with equality only for an equilateral triangle.
steps: Thus s≥√(3√3S). The equality case gives the smallest possible s and largest r.
An equilateral triangle is allowed among isosceles triangles, and its apex angle is 60°.
